units.source_text: 僧都等去后，草庵中静悄悄的。

en.t: After the priests and the others had gone, the thatched hermitage was completely quiet.

units.source_text: 夜风凄咽之时，少将等说道：“小姐在此生涯孤寂，此乃暂时之事。

en.t: When the night wind was wailing mournfully, the lesser captain and the others said, "My lady, this lonely life here is only temporary.

units.source_text: 荣华富贵之时，指日可待。

en.t: The time of honor, wealth, and splendor is close at hand.

units.source_text: 如今当了尼姑，来日方长，将如何度日？

en.t: If you become a nun now, with so many years still ahead, how will you spend your days?

units.source_text: 即使是衰老之人，到了离尘绝俗之时，也是非常悲痛的。”

en.t: Even for someone grown old, the moment of leaving the dusty world behind is terribly sorrowful."

units.source_text: 浮舟听见了想道：“现在我真是安心乐意了。

en.t: Ukifune heard this and thought, "Now I truly feel at peace and content.

units.source_text: 不必考虑为人处世之事，正是莫大之幸福呢。”

en.t: Not having to think about dealing with people or making my way in the world is the greatest happiness of all."
She felt only that her heart had grown bright and open.

units.source_text: 次日，浮舟想道：“我削发为尼之事，毕竟是别人所不赞许的。

en.t: The next day, Ukifune thought, "After all, people will not approve of my cutting my hair and becoming a nun.

units.source_text: 今日我改了尼装，被人见了很难为情。

en.t: Today I have changed into a nun's clothing, and I would be terribly embarrassed if anyone saw me.

units.source_text: 头发剪后，末端忽然松散，且又剪得不齐，安得一个不反对我的人，来替我修一修齐呢？”

en.t: After my hair was cut, the ends suddenly came loose, and it was cut unevenly too. If only someone who did not oppose me would come and trim it neatly."

units.source_text: 她处处有所顾虑，便把窗子关好，躲在幽暗的房间里。

en.t: Anxious about everything, she shut the windows tightly and hid in the dim room.

units.source_text: 她素性沉默寡言，即使在从前，也不肯把自己所思之事一一告诉别人。

en.t: She was naturally quiet and reserved, and even in the past she had never been willing to tell others everything she was thinking.

units.source_text: 何况现在，连亲睦商谈的人也没有。

en.t: All the more now, she had no one at all with whom she could speak intimately and consult.

units.source_text: 因此每逢心中困惑之时，只有对着砚台信手书写。

en.t: So whenever her heart was troubled, she could only sit before the inkstone and write whatever came to mind.
Among these writings was a poem that said:
